newsitem.title: EGYPT: US FBI chief meets Egyptian President Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: US FBI chief meets Egyptian President Mubarak.

text.p: U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation director Louis Freeh met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Sunday as part of a three-day visit to set up a Cairo office to coordinate police work by the countries.

Freeh, who arrived in Cairo on Friday on what he said was the first visit to Egypt by an FBI director, told reporters the Cairo office was an extension of the good relations between the FBI and Egyptian security officials.
"We have very good liaison relations with our police counterparts...we want to continue our good liaison with Egypt particularly in the counter-terrorism area," Freeh said.
"We have a global economy and so global crime and for those reasons in particular police have to work together. This (office) is another development in a relation that is many years old," he added.

Freeh flew into Egypt after visiting Jordan and opening a similar legal attache office in Tel Aviv. U.S. embassy officials said Freeh will also meet Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi.

An FBI official said in January a combined New York police and FBI anti-terrorist task force was working closely with authorities in Egypt after several letter bombs with an Alexandria, Egypt postmark were sent to the United States.
Mubarak has expressed doubt the bombs came from Egypt.
